title: The Ferengi's Columns
byline: by François Gautier · Voice of India · c. 2001 · subtitled A Western journalist opening his eyes to the true India
lede: François Gautier, born in Paris in 1950, was for eight years Le Figaro's political correspondent in India and South Asia. He married an Indian and has lived in India for over thirty years. These are his columns for Indian newspapers in the late 1990s. His theme is that foreign correspondents, posted for three to five years and briefed by an English-speaking elite, report India with “unconscious prejudices”. He sets out to correct that from a pro-Hindu standpoint. Ayodhya, he says, was his “political awakening”.
facts: a typical foreign posting, too short to understand India, he argues
the Hindi word for a foreigner, which he uses of himself
note: These are opinion columns written from a declared viewpoint, sympathetic to the BJP and critical of Islam, missions, the Congress and the press. They are summarised as his views.
